senses.sense_definition: Warm and formal praise or a tribute given to someone or something.

examples.text: The author received many <w>encomiums</w> for his latest novel from critics around the world.
She delivered a heartfelt <w>encomium</w> to honor her mentor at the retirement ceremony.

senses.sense_definition: A literary genre consisting of a structured speech or text that praises a specific subject.

examples.text: The classical <w>encomium</w> typically followed a strict structure to highlight the virtues of the subject.
Students studied the ancient <w>encomia</w> to understand the rhetorical techniques used in formal praise.

senses.sense_definition: A formal category of rhetoric focused on praising a person or object.

examples.text: In ancient schools, the <w>encomium</w> was taught as a fundamental branch of public speaking.
The professor explained how the <w>encomium</w> differs from other forms of persuasive oratory.

senses.sense_definition: A specific pedagogical exercise used to teach students the art of rhetorical praise.

examples.text: Writing an <w>encomium</w> was a standard exercise for students learning classical rhetoric.
The teacher assigned an <w>encomium</w> to help the class practice their descriptive writing skills.

senses.sense_definition: The eighth specific exercise within the traditional progymnasmata rhetorical curriculum.

examples.text: After mastering the fable and narrative, students moved on to the <w>encomium</w> in the curriculum.
The <w>encomium</w> serves as a bridge between simple descriptions and complex argumentative speeches.
